title: Regex Basics: matches() and Character Classes

blocks.value: A regular expression (regex) is a pattern that describes a string, or a whole family of strings, instead of just one exact value. Java's regex support lives in the java.util.regex package.
The String class's matches(regex) method checks whether a string fits a pattern, similar to equals(), but with room for variability. Compare a rigid check with equals():
to the equivalent using a regex, where the | symbol means "or":
Square brackets define a set of acceptable characters at one position. To accept both "dog" and "Dog" but not "dOg":
Add a hyphen inside brackets to match a whole range of characters, like any lowercase letter:

return word.matches("[a-z]at");         // any lowercase letter, then "at"
return word.matches("[a-zA-Z](at|AT)"); // any letter, then "at" or "AT"
The dot (.) matches any single character. [0-9]. matches a digit followed by any one character.
